correct-route-classification.critique: Two steps to judge, and this criterion scopes to whether EACH step's route matches the Rules for the work that step performs (the criterion text is 'Each step's route matches the Rules'), not to whether the step set as a whole is the right decomposition. Step 1: route 'ai_generate', app 'VoxAgent AI', action 'GENERATE_TEXT', parameters.prompt "Extract the following receipt data into a JSON list of objects with keys 'Date', 'Merchant', and 'Amount': ...". Its job is restructuring text with AI and it requires no external app connection, which is the ai_generate branch as the Rules define it ('generate, draft, summarize, translate, or rewrite text/content with AI ... with NO external app connection required'); it also uses the exact app and action literals the Rules mandate for that route ('VoxAgent AI' / 'GENERATE_TEXT'), and it correctly avoids the anti-pattern the Rules call out by name of routing text work to composio_api with an OpenAI/Gemini app. Step 2: route 'composio_api', app 'Google Sheets', action 'GOOGLESHEETS_ADD_ROW' — Google Sheets is named in the Rules as a cataloged Composio app and the slug follows the {APPNAME}_{VERB}_{OBJECT} convention. Neither step names a raw URL, an API-less portal, or a Telegram identity, so no other route competes for either. Both routes are individually Rule-correct. I record explicitly what I am NOT deciding here, so the verdict is not read as broader than it is: the trace's own metadata.rationale argues the ai_generate + for_each fan-out shape is the wrong decomposition for user-supplied (not AI-generated) rows, and steps.1.for_each is set to '{{step_1_result}}' — the same shape this case produced pre-optimize. That is a decomposition/fan-out defect owned by the fan-out-shape criterion; it does not make either step's route LABEL wrong, and folding it into this verdict would be exactly the inferential leap this criterion's wording forecloses. Confidence is held below the single-step cases to reflect that the ai_generate fit for an extraction (rather than a generation) task is the most arguable route call in this batch.
